Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise breakdown you can drop into your memo; I attached a one-page pricing roll-up and a draft mutual action plan.

Short summary (Marketplace vs Direct):

1) Billing/timing
- AWS Marketplace: charges typically appear on your monthly AWS invoice; AWS pays Redwood and consolidates billing. That means your finance team can do single-vendor reconciliation but timing depends on AWS billing cycles (usually monthly, 30–45 day settlement from AWS to vendor).
- Direct Redwood contract: Redwood invoices Acme directly per agreed cadence (monthly or net-30). Invoicing is immediate from Redwood and more predictable for our cash/collection flows.

2) Co-sell credits / incentives
- Marketplace purchases can still qualify for AWS co-sell programs, but incentives vary by partner program and require registration of the opportunity with the AWS partner team. Some co-sell rebates are tied to direct-sold deals (registered through partner programs) — we can coordinate with our partner manager to maximize incentives either way.

3) Contractual controls (SLA, data, security)
- Marketplace listings can include a link to our standard terms; however, certain enterprise addenda (custom SLAs, DPA/KMS arrangements, bespoke retention terms) are easiest to execute on a direct contract/SOW. We can implement the same security controls with Marketplace purchases, but expect a short additional attestation and, in some cases, an enterprise addendum signed outside the Marketplace flow.

4) PO & renewals
- If you prefer all-line item PO consolidation on AWS, Marketplace is convenient (single AWS invoice). If you need Redwood-issued PO numbers and direct invoicing tied to specific contract milestones, a direct contract is cleaner.

Recommended path for Acme (given Aug 1 target):
- If speed to production and single vendor billing are top priorities: pursue AWS Marketplace listing and we’ll register the opportunity and push for co-sell alignment with AWS.
- If you require custom SLAs or contract language for compliance: pursue a direct contract concurrently (we can provisionally enable access while negotiations finish).

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll introduce our AWS partner rep (Marcus) to your AWS contact to confirm co-sell eligibility and incentive timing.
- Aditya (cc) can scope any technical dependencies for early access so we can open a short-term pilot if procurement needs time.

Attachments: Redwood_Marketplace_vs_Direct_Pricing.pdf (one-pager), Acme_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx (starter MAP)
